paper: Huntington-Klein & Murray, 'Do LLMs act as repositories of causal knowledge?' (arXiv 2412.10635v1, Dec 2024 -> Journal of Causal Inference 2026;14(1):20240072, doi 10.1515/jci-2024-0072)

substantive_changes.old: Two approaches (direct, indirect), plus no-reasoning and option-order variants.
substantive_changes.new: Adds 'pick from list' (LLM picks likely confounders from a list of five; each variable shown with 3 random sets of 4 others, 10 generations each) and 'sequential' prompting (indirect cause-of-treatment question, then follow-ups, then the LLM confirms or rejects a stated conclusion). 'These four approaches ... outline our prompting approaches.' Full prompts added to Appendix B (new pp. 25-29).

substantive_changes.area: Methods: model versions for new prompts
substantive_changes.old: GPT-4o, GPT-o1-preview, Claude 3.5 Sonnet only.
substantive_changes.new: fn 4: new approaches 'use GPT-o1-pro instead of GPT-o1-preview, which is no longer available, and the claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 version of Claude 3.5-Sonnet'. Also a code error: for Claude pick-from-list, a new list of four other options was drawn every generation.

substantive_changes.old: '172 potential confounders to consider across eight different prompt variations ... a total of 13,760 LLM-generated responses each ... a total of 688 LLM-generated responses.'
substantive_changes.new: '172 potential confounders to consider across all prompt variations ... with a small number of responses lost due to non-answers for a total of 31,270 LLM-generated responses each. A plurality of these (11,760) are for the pick-from-list method ... for a total of 1,447 LLM-generated responses.'

substantive_changes.old: Direct/indirect Oct 9-15, 2024; Non-confounders Nov 23-Dec 8, 2024.
substantive_changes.new: Same, plus 'Pick-from-list and sequential prompting responses were collected between August 16 and 18, 2025.'

substantive_changes.old: Columns: Is Confounder (Dir.) 59.9/71.9/58.7; Unsure 13.8/10.2/0.0; Is Confounder (Indir.) 89.5/81.9/93.6; Related to Treatment 91.0/86.6/93.6; Unsure Rel. Treat. 3.1/7.7/2.3; Related to Outcome 93.7/93.2/100.0; Unsure Rel. Outcome 1.7/4.6/0.0 (Claude/GPT-4o/GPT-o1).
substantive_changes.new: Rows by prompt, share designated confounder only: Direct w/Reasoning 59.9/71.9/58.7; Indirect w/Reasoning 89.5/81.9/93.6; Direct no Reasoning 75.0/26.1/NA; Indirect no Reasoning 89.5/81.9/NA; Pick-from-list 47.5/44.3/41.2; Sequential 85.9/58.8/52.3. Unsure and Related-to columns dropped. Text adds 'Fewer variables, 41-48 %, were designated as confounders under the pick-from-list prompting method.'

substantive_changes.old: Fig 1 direct, Fig 2 indirect, Fig 3/4 no-reasoning, Fig 5 consistency, Fig 6 direct vs indirect, Fig 7 reasoning vs no-reasoning, Fig 8 option ordering. Distribution figures were 10-point-bin histograms with whole-number labels.
substantive_changes.new: New Fig 1 is a research-design flowchart, so old Figs 1-5 become Figs 2-5 and 8; new Figs 6 (pick-from-list) and 7 (sequential); old Figs 6-8 become Figs 9-11; new Fig 12 (pick-from-list option-position). Distribution figures are now Never/Mix/Always stacked bars with one-decimal labels (e.g. Claude Original direct 90% -> 90.2%). Values agree after rounding. New Fig 9 adds a sequential-vs-direct panel.

substantive_changes.old: 'a small share of Non-confounders are identified as confounders 100% of the time ... for more than half of Non-confounders, the variable is designated as a confounders more than 50% the time'
substantive_changes.new: 'only 21.7 % of Non-confounders are identified as confounders every time the prompt is given, but the majority (75 %) of confounders are designated by GPT-4o as confounders at least some of the time. For the majority of these, the variable is designated as a confounder more than half the time.'

substantive_changes.area: Results 5.1: new interpretation of CDPRG alignment
substantive_changes.old: Absent.
substantive_changes.new: Added: results align more with CDPRG because it is the most-discussed study; LLMs act as a database of causal links 'but not for 100 % of links ... only for the most-discussed links ... and without the ability to recognize when causal knowledge in the training data is superseded'.

substantive_changes.area: Results 5.1: new non-confounder subtype analysis and reasoning-quality paragraph
substantive_changes.old: Absent.
substantive_changes.new: Non-confounder subtypes misidentified inconsistently ('There is not a strong consistent signal'); casual review finds LLM reasoning 'generally of good quality', raising the question whether reasonable-looking reasoning is a strong marker of success (fn 7 example from GPT-o1).

substantive_changes.old: 'it designates 71% of the CDPRG (1980) confounder set ... only designates 22% of the Non-Confounders'
substantive_changes.new: '70.7 % ...', '21.7 % ...'; new paragraph: only 3.3 % of Non-Confounders are never designated as confounders by GPT-4o under indirect no-reasoning.

substantive_changes.old: Absent.
substantive_changes.new: Pick-from-list lowers 'always' shares; Added-in-2016 very poor; Trimmed/Non-confounders improve but possibly only because of fewer positives; 'all Trimmed variables are selected as confounders at least some of the time.' Sequential: for Claude and GPT-o1 'the rate at which variables are designated as confounders is similar in confounder and non-confounder (Trimmed and Non-Confounder) variable sets.' 'the changes were not consistent improvements'.

substantive_changes.old: Consistency described for direct/indirect only; 'there is not a strong pattern as to which model or method produced the most consistency'.
substantive_changes.new: Adds: consistency worst for sequential; strongest for pick-from-list ('75 % of variables reporting the same result 97 % of the time or more'). Old numbers 65.1/75.6/63.4/40.1/22.6 unchanged.

substantive_changes.area: Results 5.4: kappa for other prompt pairs (new)
substantive_changes.old: Absent.
substantive_changes.new: 'Comparisons between other prompting methods are omitted here, but in general show weak agreement. The strongest Cohen's kappa ... for GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 is 0.37 (direct vs pick-from-list, Claude) ... Several comparisons with GPT-o1 produce kappa values of roughly 0.5 ... strongest ... 0.56 comparing direct prompting to sequential prompting with GPT-o1 ... agreed for 77.8 % of variables.'

substantive_changes.area: Results 5.4: option-order and list-composition sensitivity for pick-from-list (new)
substantive_changes.old: Option-order sensitivity reported only for direct prompt.
substantive_changes.new: 'Option ordering sensitivity does not extend to the pick-from-list prompting method' (Fig 12). Other-option sets: GPT-4o rate did not differ for 80.0 % of confounders, differed by >20 % for 10.5 %; GPT-o1 same across sets for 92.4 %.

substantive_changes.old: 'highly inconsistent across models, prompts, and irrelevant concerns like multiple-choice option ordering.'
substantive_changes.new: 'highly inconsistent across models, prompts, and, for some prompts, irrelevant concerns like multiple-choice option ordering, reducing the chance that a prompt shown to be successful in a setting with ground truth would continue to work in a setting where correct answers are not predetermined.'

substantive_changes.old: No limitations paragraph; 'without a heavy signal to distinguish true-positives from true-negatives'; 'in most cases ... more than 70 %'; option ordering sensitivity stated generally.
substantive_changes.new: New limitations paragraph (single setting may not generalize; infinitely many prompts/models untested). 'with only a modest signal'; 'in many cases'; 'for one prompting method, were highly sensitive to ... order'; new paragraph: pick-from-list 'outperformed all others on consistency. However, this did not lead to improved agreement with experts'; suggests LLMs could propose initial lists for experts to evaluate; final claim now 'does not as of yet have the capability to properly designate a variable as a confounder or not'. Headline numbers (40 %/76 %, 80-86 %, 65-74 %) unchanged.

substantive_changes.old: 'This only affects Non-confounders, does not affect any GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet 3.5 output'
substantive_changes.new: 'This only affects Non-confounders for direct and Indirect prompting, only for GPT-o1-preview'

substantive_changes.area: Methods: new footnotes on design choices
substantive_changes.old: fn 3 only about indirect pairing.
substantive_changes.new: fn 3: example questions and 'expert' framing were not varied; fn 6: default token/context windows, temperature 0.7 'necessarily arbitrary', no seeds; fn 2: adherence and mortality questions asked in separate conversations; new paragraph explaining expected strengths/weaknesses of indirect prompting.

substantive_changes.old: 'We expand on this approach in several ways.'
substantive_changes.new: 'While we do not offer a formal test of whether recall is how LLMs actually do make causal judgments, our paper assesses ... and expands on previous recall-based studies in several ways.'

substantive_changes.new: Both added to the General medical examination results list.
